enriched_description: Tall graceful sighthound measuring 64-74 cm at shoulder and weighing 23-27 kg. Most distinctive feature is long, fine, silky coat flowing from body, with short hair on saddle area (lower back). Coat colors include all hues: cream, red, black, brindle, parti-color. Head is elongated with prominent occipital bone and slight stop. Ears are long, set low, and covered with silky fringing. Eyes are almond-shaped and dark. Muzzle is long and refined. Body is elegant and athletic with deep chest, level topline, and prominent hip bones. Tail is set low, carried in ring curl, and well-feathered. Legs are straight and long with large feet. Gait is free, smooth, and elastic with characteristic springy stride.

Short-legged smooth-haired hound measuring 28-38 cm at shoulder and weighing 20-29 kg. Most distinctive feature is extremely short legs relative to long heavy body creating low-slung profile. Head is domed with pronounced occipital peak and deep stop. Eyes are large, dark, and mournful with visible haw (red conjunctiva). Ears are extremely long, low-set, velvety, and trailing well beyond muzzle. Muzzle is deep and square with loose skin creating flews (drooping lips). Body is long, heavy, and muscular with deep chest and slight tuck-up. Coat is short, smooth, dense, and hard-textured. Coloration is tricolor (black, tan, white) or bicolor (red, white). Tail is moderately long, white-tipped, and carried saber-like. Skin is loose and wrinkled.

Small short-legged smooth-coated hound measuring 33-41 cm at shoulder and weighing 9-11 kg. Head is fairly long with slight dome and moderate stop. Ears are long, rounded at tips, set low, and hang close to cheeks. Eyes are large, round, brown or hazel, with gentle pleading expression. Muzzle is medium-length and square. Body is compact and muscular with deep chest and level topline. Coat is short, dense, hard-textured, and weather-resistant. Coloration is tricolor (black saddle, tan head and legs, white collar and tail tip) or bicolor (red/lemon and white). White tail tip is distinctive identifying feature. Legs are straight and sturdy with round compact feet. Tail is set moderately high, carried gaily, not curled over back.

Large powerful scent hound measuring 58-69 cm at shoulder and weighing 36-50 kg. Most distinctive feature is extraordinarily long, pendulous ears and deeply wrinkled face with loose skin. Head is narrow and long in proportion to body with prominent occipital peak and deep stop. Eyes are deep-set, dark brown or amber, with drooping lower lids showing visible haw. Ears are extremely long, thin, velvety, and set very low, hanging well below jawline. Muzzle is deep and square with pronounced flews and loose jowls. Body is powerful and muscular with deep chest, slight tuck-up, and loose skin throughout. Coat is short, dense, hard-textured. Coloration is black-and-tan, liver-and-tan, or red. Tail is long, thick, and carried saber-like. Skin texture is loose and wrinkled, especially on head and neck.

Medium-large American hound measuring 53-69 cm at shoulder and weighing 20-36 kg. Most distinctive feature is blue-ticked (mottled) coat pattern: white ground heavily mottled with blue-grey creating overall blue appearance. Head is fairly broad with moderate stop and medium-length square muzzle. Ears are long, set low, and hang close to cheeks. Eyes are dark brown and alert. Body is athletic and well-muscled with deep chest and level topline. Coat is short, glossy, and smooth. Additional markings include black spots on body and tan markings on head, chest, and legs. Tail is moderately long, set high, and carried saber-like. Legs are straight and muscular with round compact feet. Gait is free, easy, and ground-covering. Known for exceptional speed and tracking ability.

Large powerful American hound measuring 58-69 cm at shoulder and weighing 23-34 kg. Most distinctive feature is black-and-tan coloration pattern: glossy black body with rich tan markings on muzzle, cheeks, chest, legs, and ventral surface, plus two tan dots above eyes (eyebrows). Head is fairly broad with slight dome and moderate stop. Ears are long, set low, velvety, and hanging well below jawline. Eyes are dark brown with alert expression. Muzzle is deep and square. Body is powerful and well-muscled with deep chest, level topline, and moderate tuck-up. Coat is short, dense, hard-textured, and glossy. Tail is moderately long, set high, and carried saber-like. Legs are straight and muscular with round compact feet. Gait is free and powerful. Bred specifically for tracking raccoons.

Medium-large American foxhound measuring 53-64 cm at shoulder and weighing 25-32 kg. Head is fairly broad with slight dome and moderate stop. Ears are long, set moderately low, and hanging close to cheeks. Eyes are large, brown, and alert with pleading expression. Muzzle is medium-length and square. Body is athletic and well-proportioned with deep chest, level topline, and moderate tuck-up. Coat is short, hard, dense, and glossy. Coloration is typically tricolor (black, white, tan) with black saddle, white collar and legs, tan head and markings. Some individuals display red-and-white or blue-ticked patterns. Tail is set moderately high, carried gaily, and white-tipped. Legs are straight and muscular with round compact feet. Gait is free, smooth, and ground-covering. Slightly lighter build than English foxhound.

Large English hound measuring 58-64 cm at shoulder and weighing 27-34 kg, slightly larger than American foxhound. Head is broad and domed with moderate stop and medium-length square muzzle. Ears are long, set moderately low, and hanging flat against cheeks. Eyes are large, round, brown or hazel, with alert expression. Body is powerful and well-muscled with deep chest, level topline, and moderate tuck-up. Coat is short, hard, dense, and glossy. Coloration is typically tricolor (black, white, tan) or bicolor (foxhound tan and white) with bold clear markings. Tail is set high, carried gaily, and white-tipped. Legs are straight, heavy-boned, and muscular with round compact feet. Gait is free, powerful, and ground-covering. Built for endurance in pack hunting.

Medium-large American hound measuring 53-69 cm at shoulder and weighing 23-32 kg. Most distinctive feature is solid rich red or red-and-tan coat coloration, uniform across entire body. Head is fairly broad with slight dome and moderate stop. Ears are long, set moderately low, and hanging close to cheeks. Eyes are dark brown with alert, intelligent expression. Muzzle is medium-length and square. Body is athletic and well-muscled with deep chest, level topline, and moderate tuck-up. Coat is short, smooth, glossy, and dense. Tail is moderately long, set high, and carried saber-like. Legs are straight and muscular with round compact feet. Gait is free, easy, and ground-covering. Known for exceptional speed and agility in hunting. Solid red coloration distinguishes from other coonhound breeds.

Tall fast-moving sighthound measuring 66-81 cm at shoulder and weighing 27-48 kg. Most distinctive feature is long, silky coat forming profuse fringes on hindquarters, tail, and neck. Head is long and narrow with slight dome and minimal stop. Ears are small, thin, and set high, folding back against neck. Eyes are dark, oval, and expressive with soft gaze. Muzzle is long and refined. Body is elegant and athletic with deep narrow chest, arched loin, and distinctive roached back (slight arch over loin). Coat is long, silky, and wavy, ranging from white, cream, tan, red, grey, to black, often with darker markings. Tail is long, feathery, and carried in low curve. Legs are long, straight, and fine-boned with narrow feet. Gait is free, graceful, and powerful with exceptional speed.
